What we fix

Big problems. Leandersaurus-sized fixes.

Every job starts the same way: we look, we diagnose, we put the price in writing. You say go — then we work.

Broken Spring Replacement

The #1 garage door failure. When a torsion spring snaps, the door goes dead-heavy and the opener can't lift it. We replace springs in matched, correctly sized pairs so the door balances like it should.

Call about a spring →

Garage Door Repair

Noisy, jerky, slow, or just plain stuck — we track down the real cause instead of selling you parts you don't need. If a simple fix does it, a simple fix is what you pay for.

Call about a repair →

Opener Repair & Installation

Remotes quit, sensors misalign, motors give up. We repair openers across all major brands — and when replacement makes more sense, we install quiet, modern openers with battery backup and phone control.

Call about an opener →

Off-Track, Cables & Rollers

Door jumped the track, cable frayed or snapped, rollers worn to a wobble — these are the jobs that turn a small problem into a bent, unusable door if they're forced. We reset, replace, and re-balance it right.

Call about a stuck door →

New Garage Door Installation

Your garage door is the biggest moving wall of your house — and the first thing people see from the street. We install new doors in the styles Central Texas homes actually wear, measured, fitted, and balanced by a tech who does this every day. Options and total price in writing before you decide.

Why a dinosaur?

Leander's original heavyweight

115MYears old
35–40 ftNose to tail
50M yrsBefore T. rex

About 115 million years ago, a giant predator — an Acrocanthosaurus, 35 to 40 feet of muscle with a ridge of spines down its back — walked the mud of what's now the South Fork San Gabriel River, right here in Leander. His three-toed tracks are still preserved in that riverbed rock: some of the most famous dinosaur tracks in Texas.

Here's the thing: that predator stalked this ground 50 million years before T. rex — and Leander never gave him a name. So we did. Meet the Leandersaurus — our name for Acro, the dinosaur who was here first. Local, massive, and impossible to forget. Kind of like a garage door problem at 7 a.m.

Straight answers

Before you call

My spring broke. Can't I just fix it myself?

Please don't. A garage door torsion spring holds enough stored energy to lift a 150–300 lb door — released the wrong way, it can seriously injure you. This is the one garage job that genuinely belongs to a tech with the right bars and training. Keep the door closed, don't run the opener, and call us.

How fast can you get here?

Honestly? Call and we'll tell you the real window for today. We're a local Leander crew, not a dispatch center reading a script — if we can be there today, we'll say today, and if it's tomorrow morning, we'll say that instead.

Do I get the price before you start?

Yes — in writing. We diagnose the problem in person, hand you the full price, and only start when you approve it. The price we write is the price you pay.

What brands do you work on?

We service all major garage door and opener brands — whatever is installed in your garage now, we can repair it, and we'll give you straight options when it's time to replace it.

My car is trapped in the garage. What do I do?

If the spring is broken, don't force the door or keep hitting the opener button — you can burn out the motor and bend panels. Leave the red emergency cord alone unless you have to get out, and call 512-663-8867. Trapped-car calls jump the line in our book.

How much does garage door repair cost?

It depends on the door, the spring size, and what's actually broken — a snapped cable and a full spring pair are very different jobs. That's exactly why we diagnose in person and hand you the full price in writing before any work starts. Considering the quote costs you nothing: approve it, or don't.

What does a new garage door cost?

It depends on the size, material, insulation, and style you pick — the range is wide, and anyone quoting a firm number sight-unseen is guessing. We measure your opening, walk the options that fit your house and budget, and put the total price in writing before you commit.

Should I replace one spring or both?

Both, almost always. Springs are installed in matched pairs and wear at the same rate — when one snaps, the other is usually close behind. Replacing the pair now costs less than a second service call later, and it keeps the door balanced. We'll show you both springs and explain it on the spot.

Do you speak Spanish? ¿Hablan español?

Yes — se habla español. Call or text and we'll take care of you in Spanish, from the first call to the written quote. Sin problema.
